steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a paper on generating 3D co-speech gestures that follow emotion transitions in the speech. Motivate the new task and its two challenges, describe how we build the datasets and our weakly supervised approach, and finish with a bulleted list of contributions.

  - ChatGPT-4 (cite) generates transition transcripts from speech context
  - audioLDM2 (cite) for audio inpainting: timbral consistency with adjacent context, smooth emotion transition
  - then need 3D postures for the transition
- Weakly supervised approach: motion transition infusion
  - transcripts generated dynamically -> aligned real 3D pose annotation infeasible
  - weakly supervised: motion transition infusion + emotion mixture strategy
  - infusion: temporal correlation of generated head and tail gesture features = style guidance representation
  - motion transition cues infused into transition embedding via AdaIN (cite)
  - better coordination of transition gestures w.r.t. the two emotional ones
- Emotion mixture strategy, keyframe sampler, experiments
  - emotion mixture: weak emotional supervision for transition gestures
  - joint embedding of two emotional gesture sequences via temporal aggregation encoder
  - pre-train emotion classifier on annotated 3D poses with single emotion labels
  - joint embedding = emotion mixture weight for the classifier -> high-fidelity transition gestures
  - keyframe sampler: diverse initial poses as reference (output should be non-deterministic)
  - experiments on the two new datasets: vivid, emotional 3D gestures
- Contributions
  - new task + two datasets: BEAT Emotion Transition (BEAT-ETrans), TED Emotion Transition (TED-ETrans); helps 3D human motion modeling research
  - motion transition infusion mechanism + weakly supervised emotion mixture strategy
  - experiments: beats state-of-the-art on both datasets

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Co-speech gesture generation is about synthesizing vivid and emotional human postures that are coordinated with the audio input. These non-verbal behaviors are a key factor in human conversations and they help a lot with the delivery of the speech content. Modeling co-speech gestures also has many embodied AI applications, in human-machine interaction, robot assistants, and virtual/augmented reality (AR/VR). Usually many researchers focus on synthesizing human upper body gestures that are consistent with the speech audio.

But apart from a few recent works that generate co-speech gestures of a single emotion category, previous works mostly do emotion-agnostic generation. Most of them do not consider synthesizing long sequences of co-speech gestures with emotion transitions, even though these are more practical in real-world scenes. For example, a person may not keep a single emotion forever when they communicate with others or give a speech. So in this work we introduce the task of speech-driven emotion transition for generating vivid and diverse 3D co-speech gestures, shown in Figure 1. The task has two main challenges. 1) There are few datasets of 3D co-speech gestures synchronized with emotion transition speech audio. It is hard to create such a dataset with 3D human postures because there is no guidance from emotional experts and the motion capture systems are complex. 2) It is hard to model plausible and temporally coherent co-speech gestures going from one emotion to another in long sequences, especially during the transition.

To deal with the data scarcity, we present two new datasets that contain emotion-transition human speech, built on previous single-emotion ones. In particular, we first use the language model ChatGPT-4 to generate text transcripts of the transition based on the speech context. Then we use the audioLDM2 technique for audio inpainting, which makes sure the inpainted transition has timbral consistency with the context next to it and that the emotional transition is smooth throughout. After that, to support our idea of modeling co-speech gestures that are coherent with emotion-transition speech, we need corresponding 3D human postures of the transition.

- Weakly supervised approach: motion transition infusion
  - transcripts generated dynamically -> aligned real 3D pose annotation infeasible
  - weakly supervised: motion transition infusion + emotion mixture strategy
  - infusion: temporal correlation of generated head and tail gesture features = style guidance representation
  - motion transition cues infused into transition embedding via AdaIN (cite)
  - better coordination of transition gestures w.r.t. the two emotional ones

- Emotion mixture strategy, keyframe sampler, experiments
  - emotion mixture: weak emotional supervision for transition gestures
  - joint embedding of two emotional gesture sequences via temporal aggregation encoder
  - pre-train emotion classifier on annotated 3D poses with single emotion labels
  - joint embedding = emotion mixture weight for the classifier -> high-fidelity transition gestures
  - keyframe sampler: diverse initial poses as reference (output should be non-deterministic)
  - experiments on the two new datasets: vivid, emotional 3D gestures

- Contributions
  - new task + two datasets: BEAT Emotion Transition (BEAT-ETrans), TED Emotion Transition (TED-ETrans); helps 3D human motion modeling research
  - motion transition infusion mechanism + weakly supervised emotion mixture strategy
  - experiments: beats state-of-the-art on both datasets

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Co-speech gesture generation is about synthesizing vivid and emotional human postures that are coordinated with the audio input. These non-verbal behaviors are a key factor in human conversations and they help a lot with the delivery of the speech content. Modeling co-speech gestures also has many embodied AI applications, in human-machine interaction, robot assistants, and virtual/augmented reality (AR/VR). Usually many researchers focus on synthesizing human upper body gestures that are consistent with the speech audio.

But apart from a few recent works that generate co-speech gestures of a single emotion category, previous works mostly do emotion-agnostic generation. Most of them do not consider synthesizing long sequences of co-speech gestures with emotion transitions, even though these are more practical in real-world scenes. For example, a person may not keep a single emotion forever when they communicate with others or give a speech. So in this work we introduce the task of speech-driven emotion transition for generating vivid and diverse 3D co-speech gestures, shown in Figure 1. The task has two main challenges. 1) There are few datasets of 3D co-speech gestures synchronized with emotion transition speech audio. It is hard to create such a dataset with 3D human postures because there is no guidance from emotional experts and the motion capture systems are complex. 2) It is hard to model plausible and temporally coherent co-speech gestures going from one emotion to another in long sequences, especially during the transition.

To deal with the data scarcity, we present two new datasets that contain emotion-transition human speech, built on previous single-emotion ones. In particular, we first use the language model ChatGPT-4 to generate text transcripts of the transition based on the speech context. Then we use the audioLDM2 technique for audio inpainting, which makes sure the inpainted transition has timbral consistency with the context next to it and that the emotional transition is smooth throughout. After that, to support our idea of modeling co-speech gestures that are coherent with emotion-transition speech, we need corresponding 3D human postures of the transition.

But since the transition transcripts are generated dynamically, it is not feasible to build aligned, realistic 3D pose annotation of human bodies. So we solve the problem of vivid co-speech gesture generation in a new weakly supervised way, with a motion transition infusion mechanism and an emotion mixture strategy. In the motion transition infusion mechanism, we model the temporal correlation between the generated head and tail gesture features as a style guidance representation. This style guidance representation gives motion transition cues, and these are infused into the transition embedding through an adaptive instance normalization (AdaIN) layer. This way we can improve the coordination of the transition gestures w.r.t. the two different emotional ones.

In addition, the emotion mixture strategy gives weak emotional supervision of the generated transition gestures, since there is little supervision during the transition between two emotions. We learn a joint embedding of two different emotional gesture sequences with a temporal aggregation encoder. Then we pre-train an emotion classifier on the annotated human 3D poses in the dataset that have single emotion labels. The joint embedding is used as an emotion mixture weight for the pre-trained classifier, which helps synthesize high-fidelity transition gestures with desirable properties. Finally, because the generated 3D postures should be non-deterministic given the human speech, we make a keyframe sampler that produces diverse initial poses as reference. This way our method can generate diverse co-speech gestures with emotion transitions. Extensive experiments on our two new datasets show that our methods are effective and produce vivid and emotional 3D co-speech gestures.

Our contributions are as follows:

- We introduce a new task of emotion transition co-speech gesture generation, together with two new datasets called BEAT Emotion Transition (BEAT-ETrans) and TED Emotion Transition (TED-ETrans), which helps research on 3D human motion modeling.

- We design a motion transition infusion mechanism to make sure the transition gestures are temporally coordinated w.r.t. the two different emotional ones, and a weakly supervised emotion mixture strategy to enable high-fidelity transition gesture synthesis with desirable properties.

- Extensive experiments show that our method is better than state-of-the-art methods on both datasets and gives realistic and vivid co-speech gestures for emotion transition human audio.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Co-speech gesture generation aims to synthesize vivid and emotional human postures coordinated with the audio input. These non-verbal behaviors are a key factor in human conversations and significantly facilitate the delivery of speech content [1,2,3]. Meanwhile, modeling co-speech gestures has a wide range of embodied AI applications in human-machine interaction [4,5], robot assistants [6], and virtual/augmented reality (AR/VR) [7]. Conventionally, researchers usually focus on synthesizing human upper body gestures consistent with speech audio [8,9,10,11,12].

Nevertheless, except for a few recent works that generate co-speech gestures of a single emotion category [13,14,15,16], previous works mostly focus on emotion-agnostic generation [10,11,17]. Most of them overlook synthesizing long sequences of co-speech gestures with emotion transitions, which are more practical in real-world scenes. For example, a person may not maintain a single emotion forever when communicating with others or giving a speech. In this work, we therefore introduce the task of speech-driven emotion transition for generating vivid and diverse 3D co-speech gestures, as displayed in Figure 1. There are two main challenges in this task: 1) Datasets of 3D co-speech gestures synchronized with emotion transition speech audio are scarce, and creating such a dataset containing 3D human postures is difficult due to the lack of guidance from emotional experts and the complex motion capture systems. 2) Modeling plausible and temporally coherent co-speech gestures from one emotion to another in long sequences is difficult, especially in the transition duration.

To overcome data scarcity, we present two new datasets containing emotion-transition human speech, built upon previous single-emotion ones [8,13]. In particular, we first leverage the language model ChatGPT-4 [18] to generate text transcripts of the transition based on the speech context. Then, by employing the audioLDM2 technique [19,20] for audio inpainting, we ensure the inpainted transition is timbrally consistent with its adjacent contexts and that the emotional transition is smooth throughout. Afterwards, to support our insight of modeling co-speech gestures coherent with emotion-transition speech, corresponding 3D human postures of the transition are required.

However, because the transition transcripts are generated dynamically, it is infeasible to construct aligned realistic 3D pose annotations of human bodies. Hence, we tackle vivid co-speech gesture generation in a novel weakly supervised pattern, consisting of a motion transition infusion mechanism and an emotion mixture strategy. Specifically, in the motion transition infusion mechanism, we model the temporal correlation between the generated head and tail gesture features as a style guidance representation, which provides motion transition cues that are infused into the transition embedding via an adaptive instance normalization (AdaIN) layer [21]. In this manner, we can effectively enhance the coordination of transition gestures w.r.t. the two different emotional ones.

Moreover, to alleviate the lack of supervision during the transition between two emotions, the emotion mixture strategy provides weak emotional supervision of the generated transition gestures. Concretely, we learn a joint embedding of two different emotional gesture sequences using a temporal aggregation encoder, and we pre-train an emotion classifier on the annotated human 3D poses with single emotion labels in the dataset. This joint embedding is then used as an emotion mixture weight for the pre-trained classifier to facilitate high-fidelity transition gesture synthesis with desirable properties. Finally, since the generated 3D postures should be non-deterministic given the human speech, we devise a keyframe sampler that produces diverse initial poses as reference. In this way, our method enables diverse co-speech gesture generation with emotion transitions. Extensive experiments on our two newly constructed datasets verify the effectiveness of our methods, which produce vivid and emotional 3D co-speech gestures.

Overall, our contributions are summarized as follows:

- We introduce a new task of emotion transition co-speech gesture generation together with two newly constructed datasets, BEAT Emotion Transition (BEAT-ETrans) and TED Emotion Transition (TED-ETrans), facilitating research on 3D human motion modeling.

- We design a motion transition infusion mechanism to ensure the temporal coordination of transition gestures w.r.t. two different emotional ones, and a weakly supervised emotion mixture strategy to enable high-fidelity transition gesture synthesis with desirable properties.

- Extensive experiments show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art counterparts on both datasets, producing realistic and vivid co-speech gestures given emotion transition human audio.
